solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Salt and piece of food left on top of oven before tea prepared

parts.note: an ort is a scrap left over from a meal

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so the word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: the hob is the cooking surface on top of a stove
or is an old word for before, as in 'or ever'
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook leaves a scrap of food on the stove while making a pot of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is the chemist's sense: ORTHOBORATE is a salt of orthoboric acid. ORT, HOB and OR (archaic 'before') are all crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a salt is any compound formed from an acid and a base, and this borate is one such compound.

clue.text: Fast Papa has gone bust

indicators.note: something that has gone is no longer there, so the letter for Papa is dropped

parts.note: fast means quick
Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dad has gone broke, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay word; the definition is 'bust' in its police sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is slang for a police swoop on premises, the same thing as a raid by officers.

clue.text: Negotiate about splitting a pony

indicators.note: splitting something means getting inside it, so the 'about' word sits within the pony word

parts.note: a tat is a small Indian pony
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Someone haggles over the sale of a pony.
explanation.walkthrough: A tat is a small Indian pony, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to discuss terms with them, which is what bargaining parties do.

clue.text: Glorify Maggie's composure after losing power

parts.note: Maggie's means belonging to her

indicators.note: losing power means the letter standing for power, as in physics, is dropped from the word

parts.note: poise is calm self-possession
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Praise for Margaret Thatcher's calm bearing once she was out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: Maggie suggests Thatcher, but she is just 'her'.
explanation.definitionFit: To heroise someone is to make a hero of them, that is, to exalt and celebrate them.

clue.text: Robust nets end in downfall for nectar-eating insect

indicators.note: something that nets another catches it, holding it inside

parts.note: beefy means strong and muscular

indicators.note: the end in a word is its final letter, so only the last one is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sturdy net brings about the downfall of a nectar-feeding insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee fly is a hairy fly that hovers at flowers and feeds on their nectar.

clue.text: Consume more than every other character in yogurt repast?

indicators.note: every other character means taking alternate letters and skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone eats more than anyone else at a yogurt meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To outeat a rival is to beat them at eating, putting away a larger quantity of food.

clue.text: Jumpers kiss sexily in large car

indicators.note: in puts the kissing word inside the car word

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce, a large luxury car
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: People in sweaters snog passionately in the back of a big limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumpers is British for sweaters; ROLLS holds NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollnecks are sweaters with a high collar folded over, so they are a type of pullover garment.

clue.text: Trick on wharf is smarter

parts.note: a tip is a knack or dodge, a trick of the trade
a pier is a landing stage

explanation.surface: A con trick played down on the docks proves the cleverer move.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Tippy is a dictionary word for stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tippy means fashionable or stylish, so its comparative describes someone better turned out and more elegant.

clue.text: Ogle ideal boobs

indicators.note: as a verb, boobs means blunders, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A leering man stares at what he considers a perfect bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boobs' reads as a noun but works as a verb meaning errs. ELIAD is an old form of oeillade, a glance of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eliad is an amorous glance or wink, the same thing as a leering, lecherous look.

clue.text: Forget side out to restrict runs on leg

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the runs letter is held inside
out can mean disordered or wrong, so the side word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A cricket team that is all out forgets to stop runs on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words side, out, runs and leg all play other roles. In a down clue, 'on' puts the first chunk above MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To disremember is a dialect or informal verb meaning to fail to recall, which is what forgetting is.

clue.text: Scots relished it with wine

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
red wine

explanation.surface: Scottish drinkers enjoyed something with a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal, SA, is a crossword convention. SARED is a Scots past tense of sare, to savour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect to sare is to savour or taste, so the past form means enjoyed the flavour of.

clue.text: Prudish characteristic left one drifting without a date

indicators.note: to drift, in mining, is to drive a tunnel through, so these words bore into the outer pair

parts.note: s.d. abbreviates sine dato, Latin for without date
a trait is a characteristic
L for left
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A prim personality is left alone, cast adrift with no date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drifting' is not an anagram signal: a drift is a mining tunnel, so TRAIT, L and ACE are driven into SD, the bibliographer's abbreviation for an undated item.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitlaced originally meant tightly corseted, and figuratively describes someone strict and narrow in morals.

clue.text: Spirit that's immature, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak points to how a word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: vealy means immature, like a calf; the German W is said as V

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure is said to be childish.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone needs the German pronunciation of W as V. A wili is the ghost of a jilted bride, as in the ballet Giselle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Slavic legend and the ballet Giselle, the wilis are ghostly spirits of maidens who died before their weddings.

clue.text: Row about movie expressed in three lines

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
c is circa, about
ET is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An argument about a film is summed up in a three-line verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiercet, or tercet, is a group of three verses rhyming together, a triplet within a poem.

clue.text: One chum going round put on second stone!

indicators.note: going round means turning to face the other way, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: I as the Roman numeral one
a pal is a friend
s for second

explanation.surface: A friend turning round is hit by a thrown stone.
explanation.walkthrough: LAPIS is short for lapis lazuli, the blue gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis is Latin for stone and is used for lapis lazuli, a semi-precious blue rock.

clue.text: Advanced course not one to be taken up from this outdated description

parts.note: A for advanced, as in A level
a path is a course or route

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: not, then a for one

explanation.surface: An advanced course not to be taken by anyone, judged from an outdated description.
explanation.walkthrough: APATHATON is a Spenserian phrase, roughly 'apart from the path'; the definition is loose and the wordplay does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word survives only in old poetry, so the clue labels it an archaic way of describing something off the track.

clue.text: Mineral and iron bar left inside

indicators.note: inside places the left letter within the metal and bar pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a spar is a pole or bar
L for left

explanation.surface: A mineral sample and an iron rod are left in the box.
explanation.walkthrough: Felspar is the older spelling of feldspar.
explanation.definitionFit: Felspar is a common group of rock-forming silicate minerals found in granite.

clue.text: Singer holds current map for South American plateau

indicators.note: holds means the singer word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: an alto is a singer
I is the symbol for electric current
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A singer carries a modern map on a trip to an Andean plateau.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTO holds I and PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Altiplano is the high plateau of the Andes spanning Bolivia and Peru.

clue.text: You bet two pounds, for example after one

indicators.note: after places the pounds-and-example pieces behind the numeral one, so it is read second

parts.note: I as the Roman numeral one
L is the pound sign, twice
say means for instance

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers a couple of pounds on something, after the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You bet' reads as gambling but is the exclamation of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic exclamations of enthusiastic agreement, meaning certainly or absolutely.

clue.text: One set term for Michael Foot could be this

definitions.text: One set term for Michael Foot could be this

indicators.note: could be suggests the gathered letters may become something else once rearranged

parts.note: I as the Roman numeral one
taken as written

indicators.note: a term is an end, so only the final letter of the name is kept

parts.note: last letter of the name
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A political label for the old Labour leader Michael Foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the Labour Party in 1980-83 from its left wing; the whole clue describes him while its pieces are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot was a socialist on the left of Labour, and a fixed label for such a politician is this word.

clue.text: First person supplanted by European in monotony of Latin hymn

indicators.note: supplanted by means one letter is ousted and another takes its place

parts.note: tedium is dull sameness
I is the first person pronoun
E for European

explanation.surface: A European replaces the lead in a dull Latin hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of TEDIUM is swapped for E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is an ancient Christian hymn of praise sung in Latin, named from its opening words.

clue.text: Bloomers? Pilot owned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sail a ship is to navigate it
had means possessed

explanation.surface: Knickers are spotted when a pilot owns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests underwear but means things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahlias are garden flowers, and plants that flower can be jokingly called bloomers.

clue.text: Send wettest shortened messages

indicators.note: to send someone is to drive them wild, so the letters are thrown about
shortened means one letter is cut from the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to send the dampest abbreviated texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send' looks like the instruction to post messages but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweets are short posts on the social network Twitter, now X, so they are brief online messages.

clue.text: Cutting dry old schoolmaster, semi-retired

parts.note: sec describes dry wine

indicators.note: retired here means withdrawn, so half of the word is taken away

parts.note: Shakespeare used pedant for a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: A dry-humoured old teacher, now half retired, makes cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is the geometric sense: a secant line cuts a curve. Retired means removed here, not reversed: PED goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Secant comes from Latin secare, to cut, and as an adjective describes a line intersecting a curve.

clue.text: Hard to get Cliff to join church

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: It is difficult to persuade Cliff to become a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like a man's name, Cliff Richard perhaps, but is a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, so it is difficult to obtain.

clue.text: Friends perhaps enter shortly after rest

indicators.note: shortly here means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to sit is to take a rest
come in means enter

explanation.surface: Pals come in shortly after a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends is the US television series, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends was a long-running American situation comedy, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: One hugely burdened eventually taking time off

indicators.note: taking off removes something, here the letter for time

parts.note: at last means eventually
t for time

explanation.surface: An overworked person finally takes some leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlas, in Greek myth, was condemned to hold up the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan was made to bear the sky on his shoulders forever, an enormous load.

clue.text: Agitation reported, half of Doha beginning to march in Qatar perhaps

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a shake is a jolt of agitation

indicators.note: half of a four-letter name keeps its first two letters

parts.note: the first half of the city name

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A disturbance is reported as people start to march in the Qatari capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Doha is the capital of Qatar, which sits in the surface as a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is an Arab state ruled by an emir, and a territory ruled by an Arab chief is this kind of domain.

clue.text: Once went under medic on hospital department

parts.note: Dr for doctor
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A patient was formerly put under by a doctor in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went under' suggests anaesthesia but means drowned; DRENT is Spenser's past form of drench.
explanation.definitionFit: In old poetry the word meant drowned, so sank and perished in water, an archaic sense.

clue.text: To be liable to a tax initially given by region

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter only is kept

parts.note: first letter
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Whether a regional levy applies to some income.
explanation.walkthrough: Think of income that 'attracts' tax: the definition is the phrase 'to be liable to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Income that attracts duty incurs it, so the verb here means to incur or be subject to a charge.

clue.text: Frenzied shout from eBay!

parts.note: the e of the site name, for electronic
the bay of the site name, as a voe, a Shetland and Orkney inlet

explanation.surface: A wild cry of delight from someone winning an online auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The auction site's name splits into e and Bay; voe is a Northern Isles word for a creek.
explanation.definitionFit: Evoe was the cry of Bacchic revellers, a wild exclamation of ecstatic delight.

clue.text: Corps support Montgomery perhaps

parts.note: C for corps
to lift is to hold up

explanation.surface: An army corps backs Field Marshal Montgomery.
explanation.walkthrough: Corps points to Field Marshal Montgomery, but the definition is the Hollywood actor Montgomery Clift.
explanation.definitionFit: Montgomery Clift was an American film star of the 1950s, so Montgomery is one person bearing this surname.

clue.text: Manage to get a letter from Athens in front of first lady

parts.note: taken as written
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to send a letter from Greece ahead of the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: First lady reads as a president's spouse but is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage something is to succeed in doing it, the same as accomplishing it.

clue.text: Calm kid pulling face

indicators.note: pulling off the face, the front, removes the first letter

parts.note: to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: A child is settled down after pulling faces.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulling a face sounds like grimacing; here it means pulling off the front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone is to soothe or relieve them, which is what calming does.

clue.text: Millions are right about name of police district

indicators.note: about means going around, so the right letter surrounds the next pair

parts.note: M for millions
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
R for right
n for name
o' is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

explanation.surface: Millions are correct about the name of a police area.
explanation.walkthrough: Manor is London police slang for a station's patch.
explanation.definitionFit: In British police slang a manor is the area an officer or station covers, their territory or beat.

clue.text: Special treatments implicated tax official in East Kilbride

indicators.note: implicated means entangled, so the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: S for special
taken as written

explanation.surface: Special medical treatments implicated a Scottish taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: East Kilbride is a Scottish town, signalling a Scots word: a stent is a tax there.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a stent was an assessment or tax, and the official who fixed it was given this title.
